selection.question: How to choose a CT scanner suitable for the hospital?
selection.answer: Factors to consider when choosing a CT scanner: 1) Hospital size and patient volume; 2) Clinical needs (cardiac, neurological, whole body, etc.); 3) Budget range; 4) Room space constraints; 5) Technician staffing. It is recommended to clarify the main application scenarios first, then choose based on technical parameters and cost-effectiveness.

selection.question: How to choose MRI magnetic field strength?
selection.answer: 1.5T is suitable for routine examinations, relatively low cost, and simple maintenance; 3.0T provides higher resolution, suitable for high-end applications like neuroimaging and cardiac MRI; 7.0T is mainly for research. Most hospitals choose 1.5T or 3.0T depending on clinical needs and budget.

selection.question: Advice on choosing new vs. used equipment?
selection.answer: New equipment: Latest technology, full warranty, long service life, but higher price. Used equipment: Low cost, quick deployment, but requires careful assessment of equipment condition, remaining life, and maintenance costs. Recommended to prioritize certified refurbished equipment, which has some warranty and high cost-performance ratio.

specs.question: What is the significance of slice thickness and slice count in CT scanners?
specs.answer: Slice thickness determines image resolution; thinner slices mean higher resolution but longer scan time. Slice count affects scan speed and coverage. 64 slices are suitable for routine exams, 128+ slices for high-end applications like cardiac and angiography. Balance image quality, scan speed, and cost when choosing.

specs.question: What are MRI features like DWI and fMRI?
specs.answer: DWI (Diffusion Weighted Imaging): Detects molecular motion, commonly used for stroke diagnosis; fMRI (Functional MRI): Observes brain functional activity; DTI (Diffusion Tensor Imaging): Displays nerve fiber tracts. These features require specific sequences and software support; confirm equipment configuration when purchasing.

procurement.question: What certifications are required for medical equipment procurement?
procurement.answer: 1) Manufacturer needs FDA, CE, CFDA, etc. certifications; 2) Product needs medical device registration certificate; 3) Supplier needs operation license; 4) Installation and commissioning require appropriate qualifications. Verify the validity of all necessary documents before purchasing.

procurement.question: What to look for during equipment acceptance?
procurement.answer: Technical acceptance: Check functions and performance indicators item by item against contract specs; Appearance acceptance: Check equipment integrity and packaging; Document acceptance: Confirm technical documents and certificates are complete; Training acceptance: Confirm operation training is completed. Recommended to invite third-party experts to participate in acceptance.

maintenance.question: Frequency and content of equipment maintenance?
maintenance.answer: Daily maintenance: Daily power on/off check, cleaning; Periodic maintenance: Monthly system check, calibration; Annual maintenance: Comprehensive overhaul, parts replacement. Recommended to establish standard operating procedures, train specialized personnel, and sign maintenance contracts with manufacturers.

maintenance.question: How to respond quickly to equipment failure?
maintenance.answer: Establish a fault grading system: Grade A (affects diagnosis/treatment) 4-hour response, Grade B (limited function) 24-hour response, Grade C (minor issue) 72-hour response. Agree on response time, spare parts supply, temporary alternatives, etc., with the supplier.
